agency_short: West Virginia Department of Human Services (DoHS)
admin_note: West Virginia is a STATE-ADMINISTERED SNAP program — DoHS's Bureau for Family Assistance administers SNAP centrally, with no county-level policy authority (county DoHS field offices process cases but do not set policy), structurally similar to this roster's Connecticut, Nebraska, Ohio, North Carolina, and most other non-CA/NY/MN/WI/VA states. NAMING-TRANSITION FINDING this pack found: West Virginia's Department of Health and Human Resources (DHHR) was split by a 2023 legislative reorganization into three successor agencies — the Department of Health, the Department of Human Services (DoHS), and the Department of Health Facilities. SNAP is now administered by DoHS's Bureau for Family Assistance (bfa.wv.gov), the CURRENT, live source this pack used throughout — but the legacy dhhr.wv.gov domain is still actively used for some press releases and older PDF forms (e.g., some SNAP application PDFs this pack found are still hosted at dhhr.wv.gov paths), and several secondary sources this pack found still describe "DHHR" as the SNAP administrator without noting the 2023 split. FLAGSHIP FINDING this pack found: West Virginia became the FIRST state in the nation to implement a USDA-approved SNAP "Healthy Choices" waiver restricting purchase of soda with SNAP benefits, effective January 1, 2026 — see food-restriction-waiver supplement. SECOND FLAGSHIP FINDING: unlike Nebraska's soda/energy-drink waiver (vacated by a federal court in Aragon v. Rollins, June 2026), this pack found NO litigation or court order affecting West Virginia's soda waiver as of this pack's fetch date — West Virginia's restriction remains active and enforced, a genuine contrast worth naming precisely rather than assuming all 2026 state SNAP food-restriction waivers share Nebraska's litigation outcome. THIRD FINDING (confirmation of a minority-position claim): West Virginia is one of a minority of states that has MODIFIED, not fully repealed, the federal drug-felony SNAP ban — W. Va. Code § 9-2-3a (enacted by HB2459, 2019) exempts West Virginians from the federal ban EXCEPT where the felony conviction itself involved misuse of SNAP benefits, loss of life, or causing physical injury; this pack independently confirmed this is still the CURRENT, unamended statute text (fetched directly from code.wvlegislature.gov, no repeal since 2019) and additionally found a 2026 WV Board of Review decision (26-BOR-1601) applying this exact rule to a live 2026 case, corroborating that the 2019 HB2459 modification remains the state's OPERATIVE, current policy — see criminal-justice-disqualifications supplement. FOURTH FINDING: West Virginia's ABAWD work-requirement waiver situation is a genuine structural finding worth flagging: West Virginia has a long history of holding a STATEWIDE ABAWD waiver due to persistently high unemployment in its Appalachian coal counties, but this pack found no active ABAWD waiver anywhere in West Virginia as of this pack's fetch date — consistent with the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's (OBBBA, July 2025) new requirement that an ABAWD waiver area document county-level unemployment above 10%, a threshold even West Virginia's highest-unemployment county (McDowell County, ~9.1%) currently falls short of. Confirm current operative practice with the applicant's own local DoHS office, the same caution this roster already carries for CA/NY/MN/WI/OH/NC/NJ/VA/GA/IN/TN/MO/MD/CO/SC/AL/LA/KY/OK/CT/NE.
system: DoHS's Bureau for Family Assistance processes SNAP centrally; applicants apply online through the WV PATH portal (wvpath.wv.gov, "People's Access To Help"), by phone through the DoHS Office of Constituent Services Customer Service Center (1-877-716-1212), by mail, or in person at a county DoHS field office (open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday). WV PATH also handles Medicaid, WVCHIP, LIEAP, Medicare Premium Assistance, and School Clothing Allowance applications. This pack flags a lower-confidence gap: it could not directly confirm West Virginia's current Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) dollar figures from a directly-fetched, dated primary-source table — see freshness.json.
